extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders, commenters, manufacturers, regulators, and researchers interested in federal regulatory documents about vaping and flavored tobacco products
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register search-results aggregation of documents related to vaping and flavors, compiled to locate regulatory notices, proposed and final rules, guidance, and investigations relevant to ENDS/flavored-tobacco policy and compliance. Useful as a source set for preparing notice-and-comment input, compliance planning, or research.

rubrics_metrics.name: ITC complaint grounds for ENDS import violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations forming the basis for a section 337 complaint regarding ENDS imports: (1) violations of the Prevent All Cigarette Trafficking Act (PACT Act), 15 U.S.C. 375 et seq.; (2) violations of state and/or local flavor bans; (3) violations of state directory requirements; and (4) non-compliance with state and/or local excise taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These grounds are cited as reasons to request the Commission to institute an investigation and seek remedial orders (general or limited exclusion orders and cease-and-desist orders) and possible bonding. (From ITC notice excerpt: complaint alleges importation/sale of ENDS by reason of unfair methods based on PACT Act, flavor bans, directory requirements, excise tax non-compliance.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of ENDS and scope (products, components, liquids, accessories)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ENDS is any electronic device that, through an aerosolized solution, delivers nicotine, flavor, or any other substance to the user inhaling from the device; examples include e-cigarettes, e-hookahs, e-cigars, vape pens, advanced refillable vaporizers, electronic pipes. Provisions relating to ENDS extend to any component, liquid, part, or accessory of an ENDS, regardless of whether sold separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definitional criterion determines the regulatory and enforcement scope (e.g., mailability, deeming rule coverage) and appears across Postal Service and FDA documents. (Verbatim from Treatment of E-Cigarettes in the Mail and related FDA deeming excerpts.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailability restrictions for ENDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic nicotine delivery systems are generally nonmailable, similar to cigarettes and smokeless tobacco, subject to specified statutory exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postal regulations (Publication 52 revisions) incorporate statutory restrictions that generally prohibit mailing ENDS except where exceptions apply; the definition of ENDS (see above) is used to determine what items are nonmailable, including components and e-liquids. (From Treatment of E-Cigarettes in the Mail.)

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA enforcement prioritization factors for ENDS without premarket authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will prioritize enforcement resources for marketing of ENDS products that lack premarket authorization based on demonstrated public-health priorities, including youth attraction and product features associated with youth use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors cited include evidence that youth are particularly attracted to flavored ENDS products; youth preference for cartridge-based ENDS that are easy to conceal, may have high nicotine content, and are manufactured at scale. The guidance document explains how FDA intends to prioritize actions (Enforcement Priorities for ENDS and Other Deemed Products on the Market Without Premarket Authorization).

rubrics_metrics.name: PMTA content requirements (physical aspects, health-risk data, characterizing flavor identification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Premarket Tobacco Product Applications must contain sufficient information for FDA to determine whether a marketing granted order should be issued, including detailed information on the physical aspects of a tobacco product and full reports of investigations demonstrating potential health risks. For the characterizing flavor item, applicants must identify whether the product has no characterizing flavor or a particular characterizing flavor (state 'none' if no flavor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule codifies expectations so FDA can quickly check CTP's purview and identify the specific product; examples show how flavor items should be reported. The PMTA may allow alternative formats in certain instances to reduce burden for modifications or resubmissions. (From PMTA and Recordkeeping Requirements excerpts.)

rubrics_metrics.name: PMTA procedural and recordkeeping requirements (submission, filing, inspections, postmarket reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural requirements for PMTAs include application acceptance and filing procedures, inspections, and postmarket reporting obligations; manufacturers must also maintain records establishing that their tobacco products are legally marketed (e.g., documents showing a product is not required to undergo premarket review or has received authorization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule codifies FDA's general procedures for evaluating PMTAs and creates postmarket reporting requirements for applicants that receive marketing granted orders. It also addresses allowing alternative formats for some submissions to reduce burden. (From PMTA final/proposed rule excerpts.)

rubrics_metrics.name: PMTA evidence expectations regarding flavors and nicotine concentrations (bridging)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA recognizes that data from product variants can be bridged: e.g., 'X-flavor' e-liquids with varying nicotine concentrations may show health risks across concentrations without unique studies for each concentration if subset data (low, middle, high) can be bridged to other concentrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a pathway to reduce study burden when demonstrating risk across a family of flavored products and nicotine strengths, and examples are provided for how bridging might be used to support PMTA submissions. (From PMTA proposed rule excerpt about 'X-flavor' bridging.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial Equivalence (SE) report content and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: SE reports must include information to demonstrate whether a new tobacco product is substantially equivalent to a predicate product, including identification of changes that impact characterizing flavor (e.g., removal of menthol or removal of cherry flavor), changes to components, and other material changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule provides additional information on content/format of SE Reports and establishes procedures FDA will follow when evaluating them, including communications with applicants and confidentiality of data. Examples of reportable changes include removal of a characterizing flavor or changing materials of components. (From Content and Format of SE Reports final rule excerpts.)

rubrics_metrics.name: ANPRM topics for public comment on regulation of flavors
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA's ANPRM solicits information on the role flavors play in tobacco products, including how flavors attract youth to initiate use and whether and how certain flavors may help adult cigarette smokers reduce cigarette use or switch to potentially less harmful products. It seeks data, research, and comment to inform potential regulatory actions (product standards, sale/distribution restrictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ANPRM explicitly requests comments, data, and research results about flavor appeal, youth initiation, and any evidence of flavors benefiting adult cessation or switching, to inform whether to pursue actions such as tobacco product standards or sales restrictions. (From Regulation of Flavors in Tobacco Products ANPRM excerpt.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Tobacco product manufacturing practice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed requirements for manufacturers of finished and bulk tobacco products covering the manufacture, preproduction design validation, packing, and storage of finished and bulk tobacco products to assure public health protections and compliance with the FD&C Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If finalized, the rule would set forth requirements manufacturers must comply with to assure public health and legal compliance; it frames manufacturing practice expectations analogous to GMPs for tobacco products. (From Requirements for Tobacco Product Manufacturing Practice proposed rule excerpt.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Vape shop manufacturer determination criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Vape shops that sell ENDS devices and accessories are not automatically manufacturers, but may be considered tobacco product manufacturers if they engage in manufacturing activities such as custom mixing of e-liquids or other activities defined as manufacturing under the Deeming Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The distinction depends on activities beyond retail sales; the Deeming Rule and proposed manufacturing practice rule clarify that some vape-shop activities (e.g., custom mixing) could trigger manufacturer obligations. (From Requirements for Tobacco Product Manufacturing Practice excerpt referencing vape shops.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and targets for FDA Tobacco Product Manufacturing Facility Visits
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA's facility visits program targets facilities involved in manufacturing newly deemed tobacco products and components, including laboratory testing operations, manufacturing of components, parts, flavors, casings, and e-liquids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program invites parties to submit requests to participate; facility types listed include ENDS manufacturing, laboratory testing facilities (third-party or in-house), and facilities for manufacturing components and flavors. (From Tobacco Product Manufacturing Facility Visits notice excerpt.)

rubrics_metrics.name: FTC flavor data collection expectations and concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: FTC proposed information collection from e-cigarette manufacturers, distributors, and marketers to obtain data on annual sales, marketing expenditures, and data that differentiate among flavors; industry commenters noted lack of standardized methods to report flavors and subjectivity in characterizing flavors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FTC intends to collect differentiated flavor data given potential importance of flavors for trial and youth use, but recognizes industry concerns about subjectivity and reporting burden; the collection would use compulsory process orders to a limited set of firms. (From FTC Agency Information Collection Activities notice excerpt.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for classification of tobacco-derived products as drugs, devices, or combination products
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a product made or derived from tobacco is regulated as a drug, device, or combination product depends on intended uses — i.e., the circumstances in which the product is intended for human consumption and the claims or uses that indicate a drug/device pathway rather than being regulated as a tobacco product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA's final rule describes the circumstances that bring a tobacco-derived product under drug/device/combination regulation to guide regulated industry and avoid consumer confusion; examples note that vaping hardware and components satisfy the definition of a tobacco product when intended for nicotine delivery. (From Clarification of When Products Made or Derived From Tobacco Are Regulated as Drugs, Devices, or Combination Products.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Product standard proposal to prohibit menthol as a characterizing flavor in cigarettes
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed tobacco product standard would prohibit menthol as a characterizing flavor in cigarettes to reduce appeal and ease of use, particularly among youth and young adults, and to reduce tobacco-related disease and health disparities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA describes expected benefits such as reduced initiation among youth, decreased consumption among current menthol smokers, and increased cessation likelihood; the proposed standard is presented as part of a comprehensive approach to reduce tobacco-related morbidity and mortality. (From Tobacco Product Standard for Menthol in Cigarettes proposed rule excerpt.)
